name: The Western Union Co.
reason: Secular decline in agent-based remittance (revenue CAGR -3.0% over 10y, EPS CAGR 0.5%) with digital competitors eroding share and consensus FY1 EPS -27.5%; a cheap melting ice cube, not special.

name: Blackbaud, Inc.
reason: Entrenched vertical-software leader for nonprofits (Raiser's Edge/Financial Edge) with high switching costs; adj EPS CAGR 11.5% over 10y, EBIT margin up from -2.6% (2022) to 19.6% on cloud/pricing, net debt/EBITDA 1.2x and buybacks at 52% of FCF give a plausible 7%+ route; watch GAAP-vs-adjusted gap and AI/CRM disruption.

name: Willdan Group, Inc.
reason: Project-based energy-efficiency/engineering consulting dependent on utility and government program spending; growth partly bought (acq/FCF 1.08x, shares +6.4%/yr) and EPS doubled to a 10y high in 2025 after a -43% 2022, so hard to forecast.

name: Blue Bird Corp.
reason: School-bus maker at a cyclical/pricing peak: EPS at 10y max and EBIT margin 11.3% vs 4.0% 10y average after a loss in 2022, with EV mix tied to federal subsidies.

name: PennyMac Financial Services, Inc.
reason: Mortgage originator/servicer whose earnings swing with rates and refi volumes (EPS 20.92 in 2020 to 2.74 in 2023) and net debt/EBITDA ~10x.

name: KBR, Inc.
reason: Government services plus energy-technology licensing in the middle of a planned separation, with acquisition-fed growth (acq/FCF 1.28x) and a large adjusted-vs-GAAP gap; margin at 10y high 10.0%.

name: First Solar, Inc.
reason: Solar module maker whose profits rest on IRA 45X credits and tariff policy plus module pricing; EBIT margin 32% (91st pctile) vs 15% average and negative 10y FCF conversion.

name: Axalta Coating Systems Ltd.
reason: Refinish coatings is a decent oligopoly, but the pending all-stock merger with AkzoNobel transforms the company, margin is at a 10y high 14.9%, ROIC averages 4.1% and net debt/EBITDA is 2.5x.

name: Alpha Metallurgical Resources, Inc.
reason: Met-coal miner driven by steel/coal prices: EPS swung from 78.13 (2022) to -4.33 (2025).

name: Origin Bancorp, Inc.
reason: Ordinary regional bank with ROE averaging 8.6% and EPS at 0.52x its 2021 peak; no evident franchise edge.

name: Ecovyst, Inc.
reason: Sulfuric-acid regeneration/commodity chemicals with EPS down 17%/yr over 5y (0.39 in 2025), 10y ROIC ~0.5% and portfolio reshaping via deals.

name: Phibro Animal Health Corp.
reason: EPS jump to a 10y high (3.22) came from buying Zoetis's medicated-feed-additive portfolio (acq/FCF 1.56x, net debt/EBITDA 2.8x) and the core faces regulatory risk on antibiotic feed additives (e.g., carbadox).

name: StoneX Group, Inc.
reason: Well-run but earnings depend on commodity/FX volatility, trading volumes and interest on client balances; thin 1.4% EBIT margin and net debt/EBITDA 7.1x on a brokerage balance sheet.

name: ADMA Biologics, Inc.
reason: Plasma-derived immunoglobulin producer profitable only since 2024, concentrated on Asceniv, with shares up 37%/yr over 10y; too short a record to forecast 5-10 years.

name: Super Micro Computer, Inc.
reason: Low-margin AI server assembler with governance/accounting history (2024 auditor resignation), customer and supplier concentration and negative 10y FCF conversion.

name: First Interstate BancSystem, Inc.
reason: Acquisition-built regional bank (shares +8.5%/yr) with EPS CAGR only 4.5% and ROE ~8.9%; ordinary.

name: Voya Financial, Inc.
reason: Retirement/asset-management/benefits earnings tied to markets and spreads with revenue shrinking 3.2%/yr; EPS growth came mostly from buybacks (shares -8.1%/yr) and the insurer balance sheet is opaque.

name: TriNet Group, Inc.
reason: PEO with sticky SMB clients and heavy buybacks, but earnings hinge on health-claims cost trends that hit EPS -32% in 2024 (now 0.61x peak) and competition from ADP/Rippling/Justworks.

name: Delta Air Lines, Inc.
reason: Best-in-class airline but earnings are set by fuel, the travel cycle and capacity; EPS 10y CAGR 2.4% with a loss in 2020-21.

name: Cinemark Holdings, Inc.
reason: Theatrical exhibition in structural decline vs streaming, EPS at 0.46x its 10y peak and net debt/EBITDA 4.9x.
